rulings.topic: PHASE-ROLL: one spin revolution can serve all eight direction cells
rulings.ruling: A full 360-degree spin loop is direction-agnostic under a FIXED camera: over one revolution the figure cycles through every facing, so attack_S and attack_N differ only in which phase sits at frame 0. The cells loop, so phase is free — one approved 12-frame revolution can be rolled (numpy roll of the frame order) into all eight cells: 12 frames = 30 deg per frame, so N/E/S/W land exactly (3 frames apart) and the diagonals sit 15 deg off, invisible at 0.40 s per turn. CONSEQUENCES: (a) the redesign costs 1 seed + 1 clip instead of 5 + 5 — material under the Grok budget halt; (b) it makes the eight attack cells PERFECTLY consistent with each other, which is the property Matt ruled matters most (consistency over angle, 2026-09-20 camera observation); (c) the cost is that no direction gets a bespoke body lean. RECOMMENDATION: phase-roll. Matt rules at the first clip.

rulings.topic: TURNAROUND-AS-SPIN — build the revolution from deliberate stills, not from a 6-second clip
rulings.ruling: Four image_to_video passes each won the attribute the prompt led with and relaxed the rest: p1 stance-no-spin; r1 spin-no-stance-plus-zoom; r2 spin+stance+scale+NO BLUR but the mace raised beside the helm; r3 arm locked out but the spin rate collapsed and the blur returned. The medium will not hold four simultaneous constraints through 145 generated frames. RULING: a whirlwind and a TURNAROUND are the same artifact — a figure rotating in place at a fixed stance. So draw the revolution as EIGHT stills at 45 degrees (Grok stills are controllable: the battle-stance seed landed in three tries and identity carries by reference), gate every frame by eye, and register them with the frozen vc.register (height normalised, sole row anchored) which exists precisely to remove still-to-still jitter. 8 frames = one revolution = 20 fps at the ruled 2.5 rev/s. Composes with R-C8-4: this single revolution phase-rolls into all eight direction cells. COST: 7 stills (frame 00 = the approved S_battle_p3) against unbounded clip re-rolls. RISK: per-frame jitter, and the two profile views where a horizontal mace foreshortens to almost nothing — both judged at the eye gate.

rulings.topic: Whirlwind VFX port — re-express the 3D mint in 2D, carrying its design rules, fitted by measurement
rulings.ruling: Matt: load the EoR Warlord whirlwind VFX onto the pixel Warlord, fitted to the character; reference ww7-gate2-cadence-ab-plk0665. The source (reincarnated-godot/scripts/wwcr_whirlwind.gd, drax clean-room mint WW-AB) is Node3D — meshes, pooled lights, 3D radii — and the cliffside scene is 2D, so this is a RE-EXPRESSION, not a load. What must survive, because it is the design and it was expensive: the ribbon is generated from the WEAPON POSITION and is the only lit/tinted continuous thing; it is an ARC (~150 deg), NEVER a closed ring (a ring reads as a field, not a trail); everything at larger radius is discrete, brief and NEUTRAL (SCUFF_COLOR 0.62/0.60/0.56, never tinted); the trail never renders over the caster lower body. FIT BY MEASUREMENT, not by eye (runs/C-8/vfx_fit.json, canvas 512): figure height 239 px, body centre (252,270), mace reach median 187 px = 0.78 of height -> R_TRAIL 187 px; R_ENGAGE 278 px, preserving the source ratio 3.5150/2.3598 = 1.4895. Anchoring on the MACE REACH rather than on 1.9x height is deliberate: the source measured 1.9x on a realistically-proportioned rig, and this is a chibi overworld figure where height is the wrong invariant — the ribbon is generated from the weapon, so the weapon is what should set the radius. TWO 2D-NATIVE PROBLEMS routed with the piece: the sweep circle projects as an ELLIPSE under the elevated camera (squash derived from the scene ground plane, not picked); and Z-ORDER SPLIT — far half of the arc behind the sprite, near half in front — is the 2D form of the 3D disjoint-band inequality, and is what will sell the character standing INSIDE the whirlwind. Sync: one revolution per 0.400 s attack loop, phase-locked to the animation frame. Executed by drax as a post-export patch (frozen exporter untouched).

rulings.topic: Spin sense reversed to counter-clockwise (right-handed swing); mirrored-handedness fix DEFERRED by Matt
rulings.ruling: Matt, two observations on the otherwise-accepted build. (1) HANDEDNESS: some walk frames read left-handed. Confirmed — cause is the mirror set W<-E, SE<-SW, NW<-NE; a horizontal flip swaps which hand carries the shield and which the mace, affecting 15 cells (3 directions x idle/walk/run/jump/cast). The attack is NOT affected: the phase-roll reuses one unmirrored revolution, so all eight attack facings are already right-handed — a side effect of the technique, not foresight. Only fix is native generation of those three directions: 15 clips for all states, 9 for walk+run+idle. MATT RULING: HOLD until he selects an animation style. Not worked around, not partially patched. (2) SPIN SENSE: a right-hander sweeps forehand from right across to left and the body keeps turning LEFT, so the natural whirlwind is counter-clockwise; right-handed hammer and discus throwers rotate counter-clockwise seen from above. Ours was a repeated backhand. FIXED AT ZERO GENERATION COST by playing the 16-frame revolution in REVERSE FRAME ORDER — reversal flips the rotational sense while PRESERVING handedness, where mirroring would have flipped the sense and broken the hands, i.e. precisely the defect in (1). Phase offsets inverted with it: roll = (15 - 2k) mod 16. Exported warlord5; proof clean (import 0 errors, 8/8 walks, jump, cast contact, attack 8/8 with 16 distinct frames and 0.0 px drift). VFX sign flip routed to drax, whose runtime sense assertion is the verification — construction and arithmetic are not evidence about what renders.

rulings.topic: Cliffside to the loadout web app as a PLAYABLE Godot web build with a character toggle; production push authorised
rulings.ruling: Matt ruled two forks. (1) SCOPE: playable Godot HTML5 build embedded in the loadout app — chosen over the recommended lighter sprite-viewer, knowingly (the option named the wasm payload and the mobile cost). Toggle switches which of Warlord / Keeper / Necromancer you control. (2) DEPLOY: STRAIGHT TO PRODUCTION, over the recommended preview-URL-first. PUSH AUTHORISATION RECORDED HERE, not only in the session that received it, per the CLAUDE.md conflict rule: this grants a production push to reincarnated-loadout FOR THIS PIECE ONLY. It does not establish a standing pattern for loadout, and does not extend to reincarnated-demo or any later piece — those remain a fresh ask. Routed to drax. Material: Warlord C-8 48 cells (the only one with attack + whirlwind), Keeper C-3 40 cells, Necromancer C-6 26 of 40 — N/NE/NW never generated, exporter falls back to the nearest direction, and the gap must be SURFACED in the UI rather than hidden. Conductor lean given: one project with three frame sets over three web exports, because engine wasm and scene are identical and only the SpriteFrames differ; fall back to three pcks against a shared wasm before three full exports. Two landmines handed over rather than left to be discovered: the loadout vercel.json rewrites /(.*) to index.html and will serve index.html for every .pck/.wasm request; and Godot 4 web requires cross-origin isolation (COOP same-origin + COEP require-corp), which may need scoping to the game path if it breaks other cross-origin loads. Export templates 4.6.3 present, 74 GB free.

Spin passes 2 and 3. r1 (revolution made explicit): body revolves correctly front/side/back/side, BUT the legs straightened and the shot zoomed in. r2 (crouch restated as a permanent CHARACTER TRAIT — "built in a deep squat, has no standing pose, helmet stays at the same low height" — plus an explicit scale pin): revolution HOLDS, knees bent, scale stable (height spread 0.17 vs 0.25), and the BAKED BLUR ARCS ARE GONE — first clean-pixel spin of the run. Remaining miss: the mace arm RAISES beside the helm instead of holding out at full reach — the model prior for "spinning with a mace" is an overhead whirl, and prose loses to it. PATTERN ACROSS THREE PASSES: whichever attribute leads the prompt is the one that survives; the others relax. Identical anti-blur wording failed in r1 and succeeded in r2, so there is real sampling variance — a targeted single-clause edit is worth a re-roll. r3 = r2 verbatim with ONLY the arm clause sharpened (locked straight, horizontal, signpost, never above shoulder).

Turnaround-as-spin, first set of 8 (R-C8-5): the TECHNIQUE WORKS — identity is superb across all eight independently generated stills, the deep stance holds in every one, the arm is locked out at full reach in 00/01/03/04, scale is consistent (figure height 516-581 px on ~550 median) and every frame is blur-free, which four clip passes never achieved. What does NOT work is ANGLE CONTROL BY DEGREES: "turned 135 degrees" does not land. The frames that came out exactly right (03, 04 = clean back views) are the ones described by WHAT THE CAMERA SEES ("the back of his helmet"), not by a number. Coverage: front x3 (00,01,07), quarter (02), back x2 (03,04), three-quarter-back (05) — nothing at either side profile. Frame 06 is a DEFECT: the fist is empty and pointing, with the mace head detached near his shoulder. Instrument note: mace screen-angle is NOT a phase estimator here — a horizontal arm under an elevated camera traces an ellipse, so screen angle clusters near 0 and 180; and the helm-band/visor proxies validated on the C-8 spin CLIPS do not separate on these stills (quoted nowhere). Eye is the instrument. Re-fired 08 (his right side), 09 (his left side, shield face-on), 10 (replaces 06) in camera-sees language.

Matt eye: "why is our weapon so high in comparison to our characters head during the whirlwind/spin?" — CONFIRMED and the cause is the conductor prompt. Pass-1 wording was "arm locked straight and horizontal at SHOULDER height... never above the helmet". On a realistically-proportioned rig the shoulder is ~0.8 of standing height, safely below the head; on this chibi the helm spans the top quarter (crown 1.000, chin/neck pinch 0.753) so the shoulder line is ~0.71 — shoulder height IS head height here, and the instruction pushed the mace as high as it could legally go. MEASURED, worse than Matt said: the mace does not merely sit high, it does not sit on a PLANE at all — pass-1 band 0.181..0.962 of figure height (spread 0.782) against the reference sweep band [0.551,0.746] (spread 0.195, SWEEP_Y 1.20 on H_STAND 1.85 = 0.649). A whirlwind reads as a weapon tracing a level circle; ours traced a scribble. This is UPSTREAM OF THE VFX: the ribbon is generated from the weapon position, so tracking these frames literally would have drawn a tangle instead of an ellipse — correction sent to drax (drive the ribbon off a level band at ~0.55, let the art converge onto the ribbon). PASS 2 ("the same height in every frame") FAILED, spread 0.786, and cost weapon orientation (fist at the spiked head in two frames), weapon count (two maces in one) and the empty pointing hand again. DIAGNOSIS: a cross-frame absolute is not a constraint an independently-generated still can represent. PASS 3 fires a per-frame, locally checkable ANATOMICAL relationship instead — fist at the pommel, spiked ball at the far end, elbow locked, arm angled ~20 deg below level from the shoulder, ball level with the belt — from which the plane follows. Instrument caveat: the farthest-from-centroid tracker measures the POMMEL when the grip is reversed, so pass-2 heights are partly wrong; the eye found the defects the number missed.

CONDUCTOR MEASUREMENT ERROR, self-caught, correcting the record. I compared our mace SCREEN-space height range (0.18..0.96 of figure height, spread 0.78) against the reference sweep band [0.551,0.746] (spread 0.195) and called it a defect four times over. Those are not the same quantity: SWEEP_Y and its wobble are a WORLD-space Y band in a 3D scene; our number is the projected screen y of a sprite. A LEVEL circular sweep, projected, is an ELLIPSE — at R_TRAIL 0.78 H with drax measured ground squash 0.60 the vertical semi-axis is 0.47 H, so a belt-height sweep PREDICTS a screen range of about 0.08..1.02 H. We measure 0.18..1.00. The mace is therefore largely ON a plane already and the apparent bobbing is mostly correct projection. What IS still wrong is narrower: on the far side of the ellipse the frames RAISE THE ARM instead of foreshortening it — correct far-side projection keeps the fist at belt height with the mace short and just above the far shoulder. Pass 3 (b0-b4) is excellent and in band; only b5/b6/b7 (the far side) show the raised arm. Two theories spent before this one; the lesson is the standing one from this run, that an instrument is valid only on the silhouette AND the coordinate space it was validated for.

METHOD FINDING, drax, and it invalidates evidence this run already acted on. His earlier verification captures awaited physics_frame: 190 files holding only 50 DISTINCT images (repeat runs of 4) — about 3 samples per revolution at 2.5 rev/s, BELOW NYQUIST for the rotation. A correct clockwise spin can alias and read backwards at that rate, so ANY direction judgement taken from those clips was worthless in either direction — including a judgement that the direction looked fine. The A/B clips the conductor forwarded to Matt are in that class. Matt eye ruled from the LIVE game at real 60 fps, so his verdicts (A smoother, B better but choppy, and the counter-rotation itself) all stand; it is our own verification clips that were unsound. New probe_capture_c8.gd captures on RENDER frames under --fixed-fps 60: 390 files, 390 distinct, period 24 frames, and the walked square closes on its exact start coordinate. STANDING LESSON for this run, now five instances deep and all one shape — an instrument answering confidently while pointed at the wrong thing: the conductor far-point mace tracker (jumped between mace, shield and helm), the screen-space vs world-space height comparison, the regex that began counting at the wrong animation, the width-normalisation that scaled a foreshortened frame up, and drax own teal-glint mace tracker which returned the OPPOSITE sense because it caught the shield rim-light as often as the mace. Every one was caught by EYE, never by the instrument. Where a number and a look disagreed in Run C-8, the look won every time.
